title: Om gutten som gikk til nordavinden og krevde melet tilbake
world: Present-day Norway in raw late autumn. The boy and his mother live in a small flat in a grey block of flats with open-air galleries along each floor, a storage shed at the end of the gallery, and a courtyard and car park between the blocks. A long bus ride north ends at a lonely road junction with a roadside motel and café, its red and blue neon glowing in the wet dark, rubbish containers at the back and a small goat pen behind the car park. From the last bus stop a road runs half an hour out onto a bare headland above the sea, to the North Wind's low grey house, lashed to the rock with steel cables. The oat flour comes in plastic bags. The magic cloth is a plain square white tablecloth. The stick is an old wooden walking stick with a curved handle.
palette: Raw November: wet asphalt, gusts of sleet, heavy slate-grey skies, a white-capped grey sea off the headland and early, blue-black darkness. Indoors, warm yellow lamplight; at the motel, red and blue neon reflected in puddles. Accents: flour white, neon red, petrol blue and mustard.

cast.name: Gutten
cast.description: En sta og rettferdig tenåring som nekter å godta at de fattige skal miste det lille de har, og som tør å konfrontere både naturkrefter og mennesker som utnytter andre.
cast.look: A small, slight boy of about fourteen with a narrow, pale face, cheeks rosy from the cold, big ears that stick out, bright blue eyes, a determined frown and white-blond hair standing up in tufts. He wears a cheap navy windbreaker zipped to the chin over a grey knitted jumper several sizes too big, baggy charcoal tracksuit bottoms, muddy canvas sneakers, a long brown knitted scarf and a battered dark-green backpack.
cast.portrait: Background: the open-air gallery of a grey block of flats.

cast.name: Moren
cast.description: En utslitt, skrøpelig alenemor i en liten leilighet som bare ønsker ro og mat på bordet, og som blir guttens moralske anker.
cast.look: A thin, worn-out woman of about sixty, a little stooped from her aching hips, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured fleece top, a darned brown knitted cardigan, grey tracksuit trousers and felt slippers.
cast.portrait: Background: her armchair by the window in the Flat.

cast.name: Nordavinden
cast.description: En karrig, nesten menneskelig vindskikkelse som virker like gammel som været selv—knapp i replikkene, men i stand til å gi gaver som kan endre liv.
cast.look: A very tall, gaunt old man, head and shoulders taller than anyone else, with a broad, weathered face, round puffed-out cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that always streams sideways. He wears a huge storm-grey hooded anorak with the hood up, flapping like a sail, whose hem and sleeves fray into swirling grey cloud and snowflakes, so that nobody can tell where the jacket ends and the weather begins.
cast.portrait: Background: his low grey house on the windswept headland.

cast.name: Motellverten
cast.description: En grådig og opportunistisk motelleier som ser magi som en forretningsmulighet, og som ikke skyr å stjele for å få en evig fordel.
cast.look: A tall, gangly motel owner of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small, hard, glittering eyes, a long pointed chin, restless hands and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red quilted vest over a white shirt with rolled-up sleeves, dark jeans, a black belt bag heavy with coins and keys, and scuffed brown loafers.
cast.portrait: Background: the neon-lit motel car park at night.

cast.name: Bukken
cast.description: En helt vanlig bukk å se på, som gjør gulldukater når gutten sier «Min bukk, gjør penger».
cast.look: A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells, with a length of blue nylon rope tied to it.
cast.portrait: Background: a wet road junction with a bus shelter.

places.name: the Flat
places.look: A small, tidy flat in a grey block of flats: one room with a kitchen corner, a small square kitchen table with two chairs, a worn brown armchair with a crocheted blanket by the window, a narrow hallway with coat hooks by the front door, a window onto the open-air gallery and a few potted plants on the sill. Poor and worn, but cared for.

cover.prompt: A narrow road runs out along a bare, windswept headland to a low grey house lashed to the rock with steel cables, at the very edge of a white-capped grey sea. The Boy walks out along it, leaning hard into a northerly gale, his scarf and tufty hair blown straight back. On the steps of the house far ahead stands the North Wind, his huge hooded jacket flapping like a sail and fraying into cloud.
cover.caption: Derfra var det en halvtime å gå, i motvind.
cover.alt: Gutten går ut langs et værhardt nes i sterk motvind. Ytterst står et lavt, grått hus surret fast med stålvaiere, og på trappa står Nordavinden med jakka blafrende som et seil.

illustrations.anchor: Den kom rett nordfra, over parkeringsplassen.
illustrations.prompt: On the open-air gallery of a grey block of flats, a gust from the north tears a plastic bag of oat flour from under the Boy's arm; the plastic splits and the flour streams out over the courtyard and the car park in a long white cloud. The Boy stands frozen with one hand held out in empty air, his tufty hair blown flat. On a neighbour's balcony, laundry flaps wildly on a drying rack. Grey, gusty light.
illustrations.caption: Gutten ble stående med hånda ute i tom luft.
illustrations.alt: På svalgangen river vinden en pose havremel fra gutten. Melet står som en hvit sky ut over parkeringsplassen, og gutten står igjen med hånda ute i tom luft.

illustrations.anchor: Moren så på ham en stund. «Ta på deg lue», sa hun.
illustrations.prompt: Early morning in the Flat. The Boy stands in the narrow hallway in his zipped-up jacket and scarf, backpack on, ready to go, with a set, determined face. In the room beyond, the Mother sits in her worn armchair with a blanket over her knees and looks at him for a long moment, then points at a grey knitted hat hanging on a hook by the door. Dark blue light at the window.
illustrations.caption: «Ta på deg lue», sa hun.
illustrations.alt: Gutten står i gangen med jakka på, klar til å dra. Moren sitter i stolen sin med et teppe over knærne og peker på ei lue på knaggen.

illustrations.anchor: Gutten ventet. Nordavinden så ut over havet en stund.
illustrations.prompt: At the very tip of a bare headland above a white-capped grey sea stands a low grey house lashed to the rock with steel cables. On its steps the North Wind has just come back out, his huge hooded jacket flapping like a sail, and holds out a neatly folded white tablecloth. The Boy stands below the steps in the gale, leaning into the wind with his scarf streaming, and reaches up for it. Low, racing clouds.
illustrations.caption: Så gikk han inn og kom ut igjen med en hvit, sammenbrettet duk.
illustrations.alt: Ytterst på et nes står et lavt, grått hus surret fast til berget med stålvaiere. På trappa rekker Nordavinden fram en hvit, sammenbrettet duk til gutten.

illustrations.prompt: Night in a roadside motel café. The Boy sits at a corner table spread with a white cloth that is suddenly covered with roast lamb, trout sizzling in brown butter, new potatoes with dill, a bowl of sour-cream porridge with cinnamon and cloudberries with whipped cream. At the next tables, four burly lorry drivers in hi-vis vests have stopped chewing and stare. Behind the counter, a small, skinny woman with a sharp nose and a mustard-yellow cardigan stares hardest of all.
illustrations.caption: Det freste ennå i smøret rundt ørreten.
illustrations.alt: På motellkafeen sitter gutten ved et bord fullt av lammestek, ørret, nypoteter, rømmegrøt og multer med krem. Fire vogntogsjåfører slutter å tygge, og kona bak disken stirrer.

illustrations.anchor: Duken lå der. Den var en duk.
illustrations.prompt: In the Flat, a plain white cloth lies smoothed out over the kitchen table, completely empty. The Boy stands over it with both hands still flat on the cloth, staring, as the truth slowly dawns on him. The Mother, who has got up from her armchair with difficulty, stands at the end of the table leaning on it, one eyebrow raised. Cold grey daylight from the window onto the gallery.
illustrations.caption: Han sa det en gang til, høyere, med kostelige og alt.
illustrations.alt: Hjemme ligger den hvite duken tom på kjøkkenbordet. Gutten stirrer på den med hendene på duken, og moren står ved enden av bordet med det ene øyenbrynet hevet.

illustrations.prompt: At the open front door of a small country bus on a windswept road, the Boy stands on the bottom step holding the Billy Goat on its blue rope. The bus driver, a heavy man in a navy uniform jumper, leans over his big steering wheel and looks long at the goat, and the goat looks straight back at him. Grey sleet blows past; the bare headland and the sea lie behind.
illustrations.caption: «Den går som hund», sa sjåføren til slutt.
illustrations.alt: Gutten står i døra til en buss med bukken i tau. Bussjåføren lener seg over rattet og ser lenge på bukken, og bukken ser tilbake.

illustrations.anchor: I bakdøra sto motellverten og myste gjennom sigarettrøyken.
illustrations.prompt: Night behind the roadside motel, among rubbish containers on wet asphalt lit red and blue by neon. Small, heavy gold coins are rolling out onto the tarmac around the Billy Goat's hooves, and a few lie glinting in a puddle. The Boy crouches beside the goat, whispering to it. In the open back door stands the Motel Owner, frozen, squinting, his mouth slowly spreading into a much too wide smile.
illustrations.caption: Han hadde sett alt.
illustrations.alt: Bak motellet triller gullmynter ut på den våte asfalten rundt bukken, og noen blinker i en vannpytt. Gutten sitter på huk ved bukken, og i bakdøra står motellverten og myser.

illustrations.anchor: Nordavinden hørte på ham uten å si noe.
illustrations.prompt: In the narrow hallway of the North Wind's low grey house, the North Wind, his hooded jacket still stirring as if in a draught, bends over a bucket in the corner full of umbrellas that have all been blown inside out, and draws out an old wooden walking stick with a curved handle. The Boy waits in the open doorway with his arms folded, the grey sea and the sleet behind him.
illustrations.caption: I kroken sto en bøtte med paraplyer, og alle var vrengt.
illustrations.alt: I gangen hos Nordavinden står en bøtte full av vrengte paraplyer. Nordavinden trekker fram en gammel spaserstokk, og gutten venter i døra med armene i kors.

illustrations.anchor: Etter en halvtime kom motellverten listende fra kontoret.
illustrations.prompt: Night in the dim motel reception, lit only by a glowing vending machine and a small green emergency light. The Boy lies on a bench under the window, snoring with his mouth open, the old walking stick leaning against the wall within reach. The Motel Owner tiptoes out of his office in his socks with a lookalike stick in one hand and bends over the bench, stretching out the other hand towards the real stick. Unseen by him, one of the Boy's eyes has opened.
illustrations.caption: Han la seg på benken og begynte å snorke, jevnt og tålmodig.
illustrations.alt: Om natta ligger gutten og snorker på en benk i resepsjonen, med stokken lent mot veggen. Motellverten lister seg fram med en stokk som ligner, og strekker seg etter guttens stokk.

illustrations.anchor: Moren så det. Og da trodde hun det.
illustrations.prompt: Evening in the Flat, warm with lamplight. On the kitchen table the white cloth is suddenly laden with roast lamb, trout in brown butter, new potatoes, sour-cream porridge and cloudberries with cream. The Mother sits at the table with her hands pressed to her cheeks, her eyes wide, believing it at last. The Boy stands beside her, grinning, the old walking stick leaning by the door, and the Billy Goat peers in from the hallway.
illustrations.caption: Det var ikke dårlig betalt for tre poser havremel.
illustrations.alt: Hjemme er duken på kjøkkenbordet full av lammestek, ørret, rømmegrøt og multer med krem. Moren holder seg for kinnene og tror det endelig, og gutten smiler. Fra gangen kikker bukken inn.
